key_points.text: Indeterminate pulmonary nodules (IPNs) are commonly encountered in interventional pulmonary practices. The challenge lies in how to proceed with diagnosis and man- agement. Radiographic characteristics can help differenti- ate benign from malignant nodules. Several risk- stratiﬁcation models have been developed based on the prevalence of cancer among different populations and can help determine the pretest probability of cancer (pCA). The American College of Chest Physicians (ACCP) and British Thoracic Society (BTS) have published guidelines incorporating the use of pCA to determine the next steps in diagnosis and treatment. Molecular biomarkers have been developed as additional diagnostic tools to determine risk of malignancy. Finally, obtaining a diagnosis requires a thoughtful approach to the technology available, the technique utilized, and appropriate patient selection to optimize diagnostic yield.
key_points.source_excerpt: Abstract Indeterminate pulmonary nodules (IPNs) are commonly encountered in interventional pulmonary practices. The challenge lies in how to proceed with diagnosis and man- agement.

key_points.text: The first step is to risk stratify IPNs using the model most appropriate to your setting.

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT nodule size and malignancy risk percentages
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Estimate malignancy probability from size on CT
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Measure maximal diameter of the nodule on CT
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Smaller nodules are more likely benign
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Initial risk assessment of indeterminate pulmonary nodules on CT
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: probability of malignancy for nodules <6 mm around 1%, and for those 6–8 mm between 1% and 2%, respectively

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT nodule density classification (solid vs subsolid; part-solid vs ground glass)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify nodule type to inform risk and management
criteria_or_scoring: subsolid (SSN) subdivided into part-solid and ground glass
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess nodule density on CT and classify
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Prevalence of malignancy and growth patterns differ by category
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When describing and categorizing pulmonary nodules on CT
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Nodules are divided into two categories, solid and subsolid, with subsolid nodules (SSNs) further classiﬁed into part-solid and ground glass.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Benign volume doubling time thresholds (CT growth kinetics)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate benign nodules using growth rate
criteria_or_scoring: Rapid VDT <30 days or very long VDT >400 days
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Calculate volume doubling time using serial imaging
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Suggests benign etiology when very fast or very slow growth
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Longitudinal assessment of nodule growth on serial CT
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: rapid volume doubling time (<30 days) or a very long volume doubling time (>400 days) [5].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Malignant volume doubling time range (CT growth kinetics)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify malignant nodules using growth rate
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Calculate volume doubling time using serial imaging
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Growth within this interval suggests malignancy
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Longitudinal assessment of nodule growth on serial CT
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: have a volume doubling time of between 30 and 500 days [5].

diagnostic_approaches.name: TTNB and PET performance in subsolid nodules by solid component size
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Understand diagnostic yield of TTNB and PET in SSNs
criteria_or_scoring: Yield lower unless solid component >8 mm
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Small solid components in SSNs reduce PET activity and TTNB yield
limitations: Lower diagnostic yield for SSNs with small or absent solid components
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Considering TTNB or PET for subsolid nodules
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: signiﬁcantly lower in SSNs unless the solid component is larger than 8 mm [4].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Prognosis of malignant pure ground glass nodules (GGNs)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Summarize outcome data for malignant pure GGNs
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Reported 100% 5-year survival for malignant pure GGNs
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When interpreting prognosis of pure GGNs
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: reported a 100% 5-year survival for malignant pure GGNs [4].

diagnostic_approaches.name: FDG-PET diagnostic accuracy (meta-analyses: 94–96% sensitivity; 78–86% specificity)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Functional imaging to evaluate indeterminate pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: PET/CT allows functional and morphologic image capture and localization of FDG uptake
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: High sensitivity with moderate specificity for lung cancer detection
limitations: false-negatives with small lesions or certain histologies
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Common functional test ordered for evaluation of an IPN
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: sensitivity and speciﬁcity of FDG-PET to be 94–96% and 78–86%, respectively [8, 9].

diagnostic_approaches.name: FDG-PET accuracy in regions with endemic infectious lung disease
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Performance of PET in infectious endemic settings
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: FDG-PET as above
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Lower accuracy; less useful in this setting
limitations: Infectious endemic disease reduces specificity and sensitivity
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When evaluating nodules in endemic infectious lung disease areas
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: showed a sensitivity of 89% and speciﬁcity of 75% for diagnosing lung cancer, suggesting that PET is less useful in this setting [9].

diagnostic_approaches.name: FDG-PET SUV threshold
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Interpret PET uptake intensity for further evaluation
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Obtain PET/CT and measure standardized uptake value (SUV)
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: SUV ≥2.5 is highly suggestive of infectious, inflammatory, or malignant process; warrants further evaluation
limitations: Elevated uptake is not specific for malignancy
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Interpreting PET results for IPNs
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A SUV of 2.5 or greater is highly suggestive of an infectious, inﬂammatory, or malignant process and warrants further evaluation

diagnostic_approaches.name: FDG-PET uptake descriptive categories
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Alternate qualitative reporting of PET uptake
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Radiology reports describe uptake category or provide SUV
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Qualitative category conveys relative uptake intensity
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When PET reports are descriptive rather than numeric
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: PET scan results can either be descriptive (absent, mild, moderate, or high) regarding uptake or be reported as a standardized uptake value (SUV).

diagnostic_approaches.name: FDG-PET false negatives by lesion size
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Recognize PET limitations with small lesions
criteria_or_scoring: Lesions smaller than 1 cm can be falsely negative
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Spatial resolution limits detection in small lesions
limitations: Small size may yield false-negative PET
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Interpreting negative PET in small nodules
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: such lesions smaller than 1 cm, due to limitations of spatial resolution [7].

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT pseudocavitation with smooth thin (<4 mm) walls (benign characteristic)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: CT feature suggesting benign nodule
criteria_or_scoring: Pseudocavitation with smooth thin (<4 mm) walls
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess wall thickness on CT
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Listed among benign characteristics
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: CT interpretation of nodule internal characteristics
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Pseudocavitation with smooth thin (<4 mm) walls

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT pseudocavitation with thick (>16 mm) irregular walls (malignant characteristic)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: CT feature suggesting malignant nodule
criteria_or_scoring: Pseudocavitation with thick (>16 mm) irregular walls
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess wall thickness on CT
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Listed among malignant characteristics
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: CT interpretation of nodule internal characteristics
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Pseudocavitation with thick (>16 mm) irregular walls

diagnostic_approaches.name: Mayo Clinic Model (Swensen model)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Calculate pretest probability of malignancy for incidentally detected nodules
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Apply model using listed predictors to compute pCA
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Provides malignancy risk estimate to guide evaluation
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Incidentally detected nodules on imaging
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: They examined 6 independent predictors of malignancy in 629 patients with nodules between 4 mm and 30 mm. The prevalence of malignancy in this cohort was 23%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Herder Model
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Refine malignancy risk by incorporating PET with clinical/radiographic predictors
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Add PET uptake category to clinical and CT predictors
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Addition of PET improved accuracy; increases pCA when PET positive
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Incidentally detected nodules when PET is available
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: This study only included 106 patients, with a prevalence of malignancy of 57.5%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Brock University Model
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Estimate malignancy risk in screening-detected nodules
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Apply model to screening CT findings and demographics
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Performs well in smaller nodules
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Screening population nodules
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The prevalence of malignancy in this population was lower than the other models at 5.5%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: TREAT 1.0 Model
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assess malignancy risk in patients referred for surgical evaluation; avoid unnecessary surgeries
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use model in thoracic surgery clinic population being considered for resection
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Had better accuracy than the Mayo Clinic Model in this population
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: High-risk patients referred for surgical resection consideration
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: 492 patients referred to thoracic surgical clinics… the prevalence of malignancy was 72% in this high-risk population.

diagnostic_approaches.name: TREAT 2.0 Model
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate benign from malignant nodules in high-risk clinical settings
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Apply model across pulmonary nodule/thoracic surgery clinic and surgical cohorts
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Better differentiation than other calculators in this population
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: High-risk patients in specialized clinics or surgical settings
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: assess IPNs in 1401 high-risk patients… prevalence of malignancy in these cohorts were 90%, 42%, and 73%, respectively

diagnostic_approaches.name: Physician assessment of pretest probability (pCA)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Clinician-estimated malignancy risk using nodule features
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Clinician integrates CT characteristics to estimate pCA
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Outperformed the Mayo and VA models in distinguishing benign from malignant in one study
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: In pulmonary nodule or thoracic surgery clinics
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: clinician estimated pCA outperformed the Mayo and VA models… in a population of 337 patients with a cancer prevalence of 47%

diagnostic_approaches.name: Lung-RADS classification (screening CT reporting)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Standardize reporting and risk categorization for lung cancer screening CT
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assign Lung-RADS category to screening CT finding
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: As Lung-RADS score increases, cancer detection rate increases
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Lung cancer screening CT reporting
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Lung RADS categorizations are as follows: 1 and 2 (negative), 3 (probably benign), 4A (suspicious), 4B (very suspicious), and 4X…

diagnostic_approaches.name: Volumetric growth definition (pulmonary nodule)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Define radiographic growth between serial CT scans
criteria_or_scoring: Growth is defined as a volume increase of at least 25% between scans
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess nodule volume change on serial CT scans
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: ≥25% volume increase indicates growth
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When comparing serial CT scans during surveillance
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Growth is defined as a volume increase of at least 25% between scans [5].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nodule Volume Doubling Time (VDT) cutoff
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate benign versus malignant pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Calculate VDT from serial volumetric CT measurements
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Using 500-day cutoff: specificity 90%, sensitivity 91%, NPV 98%, PPV 67%
limitations: not the case for all tumors. Volumetry cannot be accurately performed in nonsolid or part-solid lesions.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: To assess changes between serial CT scans
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Using a cutoff of 500 days, the specificity of this technique was 90%, sensitivity of 91%, NPV of 98%, and PPV of 67% [32].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Serial CT surveillance (noncontrast low-dose chest CT)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Imaging modality for patients undergoing surveillance
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use noncontrast low radiation dose chest CT
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: For most patients undergoing surveillance
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Noncontrast low radiation dose chest CT should be used for most patients undergoing surveillance.

diagnostic_approaches.name: PET/CT detection threshold for solid nodules
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: If solid component is greater than the PET/CT detection threshold
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: the PET/CT detection threshold, [26] which is usually >8 mm.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Blood-based rule-out biomarker (LG3BP and C163A with clinical factors)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Rule-out test to assess malignancy risk in intermediate risk pulmonary nodules
criteria_or_scoring: C163A and five clinical risk factors (age
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Blood test with integrated clinical factors
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Sensitivity 97%, specificity 44%, NPV 98% in intermediate-risk pulmonary nodules 8–30 mm
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Intermediate risk pulmonary nodules 8–30 mm in size
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: demonstrated a sensitivity of 97%, specificity of 44%, and a negative predictive value (NPV) of 98% in patients presenting with intermediate risk pulmonary nodules 8–30 mm in size [37].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Seven-autoantibody panel
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify malignant lung nodules
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Increased the risk of malignancy 2.7-fold in intermediate risk nodules 4–20 mm
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Intermediate risk nodules 4–20 mm in size
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: When applied to intermediate risk nodules 4–20 mm in size, a seven-autoantibody panel was shown to increase the risk of malignancy 2.7-fold [39].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Nasal swab genomic classifier (nasal squamous epithelium)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Evaluate the probability of lung cancer in patients with IPNs who formerly or currently smoke
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Nasal swab to obtain nasal squamous epithelium
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Low-risk: sensitivity 96%, specificity 42% (rule-out). High-risk: sensitivity 58%, specificity 90% (rule-in).
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Patients presenting with IPNs who formerly or currently smoke
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: low-risk classifier demonstrated a sensitivity of 96% and specificity of 42% to rule out lung cancer, while the high-risk classifier had a sensitivity of 58% and a specificity of 90%

diagnostic_approaches.name: Guided bronchoscopy (pooled modalities)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Evaluation of peripheral indeterminate pulmonary nodules
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Guided bronchoscopic techniques
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Pooled diagnostic yield across modalities was 69%
limitations: varying prevalence of malignancy will impact diagnostic yield.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The study found that the pooled diagnostic yield across all bronchoscopic modalities was 69%, which had not improved over 20 years [46].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) for mediastinal lymph nodes
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Had the highest diagnostic yield at 80%
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: For mediastinal lymph nodes
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: EBUS (for mediastinal lymph nodes) had the highest diagnostic yield at 80%

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoscopy diagnostic yield by pretest probability of cancer (pCA)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Relate bronchoscopy yield to pCA categories
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Lower yield (44% and 42%) in pCA <10% and 10–60%
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Nodules with pCA < 10% and 10–60% had a lower yield (44% and 42%).

diagnostic_approaches.name: Navigational bronchoscopy (VERITAS trial)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnosis of indeterminate lung nodules
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Diagnostic yield 76%; fewer complications (5.8% vs 31%) than CT-guided biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: diagnostic yield of both approaches were equivalent (76%) and navigational bronchoscopy was associated with significantly less postprocedural complications (5.8% vs 31%) [45].

diagnostic_approaches.name: CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy (TTNB) (VERITAS trial comparator)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnosis of indeterminate lung nodules
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Diagnostic yield 76%; higher complications (31%) than navigational bronchoscopy (5.8%)
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: diagnostic yield of both approaches were equivalent (76%) and navigational bronchoscopy was associated with significantly less postprocedural complications (5.8% vs 31%) [45].

diagnostic_approaches.name: TTNB selection consideration (lesion near chest wall)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Patient selection to optimize diagnostic approach
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: A 1 cm tumor close to the chest wall may be better approached with TTNB
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: a 1 cm tumor close to the chest wall may be better approached with TTNB than other bronchoscopic techniques.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchus sign (predictor of bronchoscopy diagnostic yield)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify factors associated with higher diagnostic yield
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess presence of a bronchus sign on imaging
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Presence may promote a high diagnostic yield
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When selecting patients for bronchoscopy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Other factors that may promote a high diagnostic yield include larger lesion size and presence of a bronchus sign [46].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Liquid biopsy (ctDNA or miRNA)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Noninvasive molecular biomarker to further assess risk of malignancy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: liquid biopsies identifying circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) or microRNA (miRNA)

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchial epithelial cell genomic classifiers
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Noninvasive molecular biomarker to assess IPNs
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: bronchial or nasal epithelial cell genomic classifiers

diagnostic_approaches.name: Exhaled volatile organic compounds (VOCs)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Noninvasive molecular biomarker candidate
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: exhaled volatile organic compounds [35].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Brock risk assessment model
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Risk stratification of subsolid nodules >5 mm
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Risk-stratify SSNs >5 mm
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: All SSNs >5 mm should be risk stratified with the Brock risk assessment model.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Herder model
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assess risk after PET/CT
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: After PET/CT to assess risk and determine next steps
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: After the PET/CT is performed, the Herder model should be used to assess risk and determine next steps.

treatment_algorithms.title: ACCP 2013 Diagnostic Algorithm (figure reference)
treatment_algorithms.source_excerpt: Fig. 1 American College of Chest Physicians 2013 Guidelines diagnostic algorithm.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: <8 mm without risk factors
specific_recommendations: For solid nodules <8 mm without risk factors: choose CT surveillance based on the nodule size.
decision_points_and_pathways: If solid nodule <8 mm and no risk factors: select CT surveillance based on size.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Solid nodules less than 8 mm without risk factors.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: CT surveillance based on nodule size.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In patients with solid nodules less than 8 mm and without risk factors, CT surveillance should be chosen based on the nodule size

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: Multiple nodules follow-up
specific_recommendations: If multiple nodules are present, base follow-up on the size of the largest nodule.
decision_points_and_pathways: Multiple nodules present: follow-up determined by largest nodule size.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with multiple solid nodules.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Follow-up schedule determined by largest nodule size.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: If there are multiple nodules, follow-up is based on the size of the largest nodule

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: Very low risk (>8 mm) surveillance initiation
specific_recommendations: For solid nodules >8 mm with pCA <5%, serial surveillance imaging is recommended.
decision_points_and_pathways: Solid nodule >8 mm and pCA <5%: choose serial surveillance imaging.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Solid nodules larger than 8 mm with pretest probability <5%.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Serial surveillance imaging per ACCP intervals.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In patients with solid nodules larger than 8 mm, serial surveillance imaging is recommended for patients with very low risk (defined as having a pretest probability estimated to be <5%).

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: Very low risk surveillance intervals
specific_recommendations: Schedule surveillance imaging at 3–6, 9–12, and 18–24 months.
decision_points_and_pathways: Use surveillance intervals of 3–6, 9–12, and 18–24 months.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Very low risk solid nodules under surveillance.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: CT at 3–6, 9–12, and 18–24 months.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: at intervals of 3–6, 9–12, and 18–24 months

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: Stop imaging after 2 years stability
specific_recommendations: If a solid nodule is stable for 2 years, no further CT imaging is needed.
decision_points_and_pathways: Solid nodule stable 2 years: discontinue CT imaging.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Solid nodules with 2 years of radiographic stability.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: None after 2 years of stability.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: For solid lesions that have been stable for 2 years, further CT imaging is not required.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: Intermediate risk (5–65%) initial evaluation
specific_recommendations: For pCA 5–65%: perform PET scan or nonsurgical biopsy.
decision_points_and_pathways: pCA 5–65%: choose PET or nonsurgical biopsy based on nodule size, location, and airway proximity.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pretest probability 5–65%.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: As per PET/biopsy results; consider surveillance when criteria met.
alternative_approaches: CT-guided biopsy or bronchoscopy depending on nodule factors.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In patients with low to moderate pCA, between 5% and 65%, further evaluation should be performed to better elucidate if the lesion is malignant or benign with either PET scan or nonsurgical biopsy.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: When to use surveillance in intermediate risk
specific_recommendations: Advise surveillance CT when pCA <30–40% and lesion not PET avid or ≤15 Hounsfield units, or nondiagnostic needle biopsy and not PET avid.
decision_points_and_pathways: If pCA <30–40% and PET negative/low attenuation, consider surveillance CT.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Intermediate-risk patients meeting PET/attenuation criteria.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Surveillance CT per clinical judgment.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: pretest probability is <30–40% and the lesion is not PET avid or is not more than 15 Hounsfield units

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: High risk (>65%) management
specific_recommendations: Do not use PET to characterize nodules; pursue surgical diagnosis.
decision_points_and_pathways: pCA >65%: proceed to surgical diagnosis; avoid PET for characterization.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pretest probability >65%.
alternative_approaches: Nonsurgical biopsy if tumor molecular testing needed pre-surgery.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: pretest probability is high, >65%, functional imaging (i.e., PET scan) to characterize the nodule is not recommended and surgical diagnosis should be pursued.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: Pre-surgical biopsy for molecular testing
specific_recommendations: Consider nonsurgical biopsy when tumor mutational analysis is recommended prior to surgery (clinical stage 1B–3A).
decision_points_and_pathways: High-risk with planned adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy: obtain nonsurgical biopsy for molecular testing.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with clinical stage 1B–3A where adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy is considered.
alternative_approaches: Proceed directly to surgery when molecular testing not required.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: reasonable to pursue a nonsurgical biopsy if tumor mutational analysis is recommended prior to surgery (patients with clinical stage 1B-3A) where adjuvant and neoadjuvant therapy is being considered

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: PET for staging (not characterization) in high risk
specific_recommendations: Use PET prior to treatment for lung cancer staging purposes.
decision_points_and_pathways: High-risk nodule: order PET for staging before treatment.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients proceeding to treatment for suspected lung cancer.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Pre-treatment PET staging.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: PET imaging, while not recommended for distinguishing benign from malignant nodules in this setting, is still recommended prior to treatment for lung cancer staging purposes

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: Management of growth on surveillance
specific_recommendations: If a lesion grows on surveillance, perform nonsurgical biopsy or surgical resection unless comorbidities favor SBRT without tissue confirmation.
decision_points_and_pathways: Growth observed: choose biopsy or resection; consider SBRT without tissue if procedures high risk.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with solid nodules demonstrating growth on surveillance.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: High procedural risk may warrant SBRT without tissue confirmation.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Surveillance imaging to detect growth.
alternative_approaches: SBRT without tissue confirmation when comorbidities preclude biopsy/resection.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: For lesions that grow on surveillance imaging, nonsurgical biopsy or surgical resection should be performed unless the patient has comorbidities which make those procedures such high risk that treatment with stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) is being considered without tissue confirmation

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid Nodules: PET avidity and biopsy results guiding surgery
specific_recommendations: Consider surgical diagnosis if a nodule is PET avid or if nonsurgical biopsy is suspicious for malignancy.
decision_points_and_pathways: PET avid or suspicious nonsurgical biopsy: proceed to surgical diagnosis.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with PET-avid nodules or suspicious biopsy findings.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Surgical diagnosis should be considered if a nodule is PET avid or if nonsurgical biopsy is suspicious for malignancy.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Solid/Subsolid Nodules: Shared decision-making
specific_recommendations: Use shared decision-making throughout care to align with patient preferences and values.
decision_points_and_pathways: Discuss options and preferences across risk categories and interventions.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: All patients undergoing pulmonary nodule evaluation.
alternative_approaches: Biopsy for peace of mind in low-risk; biopsy before surgery in high-risk if desired.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Shared decision-making should be performed throughout the continuum of care, in line with the patient’s preferences and values.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules: Pure ground glass <5 mm
clinical_guidelines.condition: Indeterminate pulmonary nodules – subsolid (pure ground glass)
specific_recommendations: For pure ground glass nodules <5 mm: no further follow-up.
decision_points_and_pathways: Pure GGN <5 mm: stop follow-up.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pure ground glass nodules less than 5 mm.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: None.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In patients with a pure ground glass nodule less than 5 mm in diameter, no further follow-up is recommended.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules: Pure ground glass >5 mm
clinical_guidelines.condition: Indeterminate pulmonary nodules – subsolid (pure ground glass)
specific_recommendations: If pure ground glass nodule >5 mm: perform annual surveillance for at least 3 years.
decision_points_and_pathways: Pure GGN >5 mm: annual surveillance ≥3 years.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with pure ground glass nodules more than 5 mm.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Annual surveillance for at least 3 years.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: If the lesion is more than 5 mm, annual surveillance is recommended for at least 3 years

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules: Definition of part-solid
specific_recommendations: Define part-solid nodules as >50% ground glass.
decision_points_and_pathways: Classify as part-solid if >50% ground glass.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Subsolid nodules with mixed attenuation.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Part solid is defined as >50% ground glass.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules: Part-solid <8 mm follow-up
specific_recommendations: Repeat CT at 3, 12, and 24 months; then annual scans for an additional 1–3 years.
decision_points_and_pathways: Part-solid <8 mm: scheduled CT at 3, 12, 24 months; then annual 1–3 years.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with part-solid nodules less than 8 mm.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: CT at 3, 12, 24 months; annual 1–3 additional years.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: less than 8 mm in diameter, repeat CT imaging at 3, 12, and 24 months is advised with annual scans for an additional 1–3 years.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules: Part-solid >8 mm management
specific_recommendations: Repeat CT in 3 months; if persistent/growth, evaluate with PET, biopsy, or resection.
decision_points_and_pathways: Part-solid >8 mm: CT at 3 months; then PET/biopsy/resection if persists/grows.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with part-solid nodules greater than 8 mm.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: CT at 3 months.
alternative_approaches: PET, nonsurgical biopsy, or resection after persistence/growth.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: part-solid nodule greater than 8 mm, repeat CT should occur in 3 months followed by further evaluation with PET, biopsy, or resection if it persists and/or grows.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules: Avoid PET when solid component <8 mm
specific_recommendations: Do not perform PET when the solid component is <8 mm.
decision_points_and_pathways: Solid component <8 mm: avoid PET.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Part-solid nodules with small solid component (<8 mm).
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: PET contraindicated for solid component <8 mm.
alternative_approaches: CT surveillance or other evaluation per size/growth.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: PET scan should not be performed in those nodules with a solid component of less than 8 mm.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Subsolid Nodules: Part-solid >15 mm management
specific_recommendations: For part-solid >15 mm: evaluate with PET, nonsurgical biopsy, or resection.
decision_points_and_pathways: Part-solid >15 mm: proceed to PET/biopsy/resection.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with part-solid nodules larger than 15 mm.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: If the part-solid nodule is larger than 15 mm, further evaluation with PET, nonsurgical biopsy, or resection is warranted

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Use of calculators, volumetrics, and image-guided biopsy
specific_recommendations: Incorporate nodule calculators in initial assessment and follow-up.
Use volumetric measurements for assessment and follow-up.
Provide guidance on image-guided biopsies.
decision_points_and_pathways: Apply risk calculators and volumetrics at baseline and during follow-up.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with indeterminate pulmonary nodules.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Volumetric follow-up per BTS approach.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: incorporate the use of nodule calculators and volumetric measurements in both initial assessment and follow-up.

clinical_guidelines.title: Fleischner Society Guidelines – Mentioned
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: consistent with the Fleischner Society Guidelines discussed below.

clinical_guidelines.title: Lung-RADS categorization (screening CT reporting)
specific_recommendations: Use categories: 1 and 2 (negative), 3 (probably benign), 4A (suspicious), 4B (very suspicious), 4X (additional features increasing risk).
decision_points_and_pathways: Assign Lung-RADS category based on features; higher category indicates higher cancer risk.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Screening population chest CTs.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Lung RADS categorizations are as follows: 1 and 2 (negative), 3 (probably benign), 4A (suspicious), 4B (very suspicious), and 4X (category used to up score risk of cancer

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Risk thresholds and surveillance of small solid nodules
specific_recommendations: Use Brock and Herder models to assess pCA in solid IPNs.
Risk thresholds: low (<10%), intermediate (10–70%), high (>70%).
Do not surveil nodules <5 mm or 80 mm3.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: solid IPNs
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Do not recommend surveilling nodules less than 5 mm or 80 mm3.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: different risk thresholds for low- (<10%), intermediate- (10–70%), and high-risk nodules (>70%) and do not recommend surveilling nodules less than 5 mm or 80 mm3

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Follow-up duration for low-risk solid nodules
specific_recommendations: If risk of malignancy is low (<10%), reduce follow-up period to 1 year.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: solid IPNs with low risk of malignancy (<10%)
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Follow-up period reduced to one year for low-risk (<10%) nodules.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: They also suggest the follow-up period be reduced to one year if risk of malignancy is low, <10%

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Solid nodules: volumetric assessment and VDT-based management
specific_recommendations: For pCA <10%: repeat CT with volumetric assessment and calculate VDT.
For VDT <400 days: further investigation (biopsy, imaging, or resection).
If VDT >600 days or <25% change in volume after 1 year: no further follow-up; consider yearly surveillance for VDT 400–600 days.
decision_points_and_pathways: pCA <10%: repeat CT with volumetric assessment and VDT calculation.
VDT <400 days: proceed with biopsy/imaging/resection.
VDT 400–600 days: consider yearly surveillance.
VDT >600 days or <25% volume change at 1 year: stop follow-up.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: solid IPNs, low pretest probability (<10%)
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Use volumetric assessment; consider yearly surveillance for VDT 400–600 days.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Further investigation with biopsy, imaging, or resection for VDT <400 days.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: VDT < 400 days is recommended for IPNs. If VDT is >600 days or less than 25% change in volume after 1 year, then no further follow-up is required

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Management when pCA >10% (solid component PET threshold and Herder model)
specific_recommendations: If risk of malignancy >10%: obtain PET if solid component > PET/CT detection threshold (usually >8 mm).
After PET/CT, use the Herder model to assess risk and determine next steps.
decision_points_and_pathways: pCA >10% and solid component >8 mm: pursue PET/CT.
Post-PET: apply Herder model to guide next steps.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: IPNs with risk of malignancy >10%
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: For nodules with risk of malignancy >10%, PET scan should be pursued if the solid component is greater than the PET/CT detection threshold, which is usually >8 mm.

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Subsolid nodules: follow-up threshold and risk stratification
specific_recommendations: Do not follow nodules <5 mm.
All SSNs >5 mm should be risk stratified with the Brock model.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Subsolid nodules; SSNs >5 mm for risk stratification
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Do not follow up nodules less than 5 mm.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: It is recommended that nodules less than 5 mm not be followed up. All SSNs >5 mm should be risk stratified with the Brock risk assessment model.

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Subsolid nodules: surveillance intervals and growth-triggered actions
specific_recommendations: If pCA <10%: repeat CT at 1, 2, and 4 years.
If a GGN increases >2 mm: repeat CT in 6 months.
Resection or nonsurgical treatment of part-solid nodules if solid component enlarges or develops in a GGN.
decision_points_and_pathways: pCA <10%: CT at 1, 2, 4 years.
GGN growth >2 mm: CT in 6 months.
Part-solid: treat if solid component enlarges or appears.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: SSNs with pCA <10%; GGNs with interval growth
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: CT surveillance at 1, 2, and 4 years for pCA <10%; 6-month CT for GGN growth >2 mm.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Resection or nonsurgical treatment for part-solid nodules with enlarging/new solid component.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: pCA <10%, repeat CT scan at 1, 2, and 4 years is recommended. If a GGN increases more than 2 mm, then repeat CT should be performed in 6 months.

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Risk category thresholds for solid pulmonary nodules
specific_recommendations: Low risk: <5%
Intermediate risk: 5–65%
High risk: >65%
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Management of Solid Pulmonary Nodules
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Low risk <5% Intermediate risk 5–65% High risk >65%

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Risk category thresholds for solid pulmonary nodules
specific_recommendations: Low risk: <10%
Intermediate risk: 10–70%
High risk: >70%
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Management of Solid Pulmonary Nodules
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Low risk <10% Intermediate risk 10–70% High risk >70%

clinical_guidelines.title: ACCP Guidelines – Imaging follow-up threshold and surveillance period
specific_recommendations: Threshold for follow-up imaging: >6 mm.
Surveillance period: 2 years.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Management of Solid Pulmonary Nodules
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Surveillance period 2 years for nodules above threshold.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Threshold for follow-up imaging >6 mm Surveillance period 2 years

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Imaging follow-up threshold and surveillance period
specific_recommendations: Threshold for follow-up imaging: >80 mm3 or >6 mm diameter.
Surveillance period: 1 year.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Management of Solid Pulmonary Nodules
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Surveillance period 1 year for nodules above threshold.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Threshold for follow-up imaging >80 mm3 or > 6 mm diameter Surveillance period 1 year

clinical_guidelines.title: Fleischner Society Guidelines – Evaluation threshold by cancer risk
specific_recommendations: Limit evaluation if probability of lung cancer <1%.
Encourage further evaluation when risk >1%.
decision_points_and_pathways: <1% risk: limit evaluation.
>1% risk: pursue further evaluation.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Incidentally detected IPNs; not for screen-detected nodules.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: aim to limit unnecessary evaluation of patients with less than 1% probability of lung cancer and encourages further evaluation when the risk is greater than 1% for IPNs

clinical_guidelines.title: Fleischner Society Guidelines – Size-based follow-up recommendations
specific_recommendations: Provides surveillance intervals for nodules <6 mm if patient is high risk.
Recommends risk categorization for nodules >8 mm.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Incidentally detected IPNs; high-risk patients; nodules >8 mm
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Surveillance intervals for nodules <6 mm in high-risk patients (details per guideline).
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: It provides surveillance intervals for nodules less than 6 mm if a patient is high risk and recommends risk categorization for nodules greater than 8 mm.

clinical_guidelines.title: BTS Guidelines – Use of Brock and Herder models in solid IPNs
specific_recommendations: Utilize both the Brock and the Herder model to assess pCA in the algorithm for evaluation and management of solid IPNs.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: solid IPNs
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The BTS guidelines specifically utilize both the Brock and the Herder model to assess pCA in their algorithm for evaluation and management of solid IPNs

clinical_guidelines.title: Standard of care for high pCA nodules – surgical referral and alternatives
clinical_guidelines.condition: indeterminate pulmonary nodules with high probability of malignancy
specific_recommendations: For pCA >65%: refer to surgery for resection if operable.
Nonsurgical biopsy may be performed prior to surgical evaluation.
If not surgical candidate or biopsy nondiagnostic/not possible: offer SBRT.
decision_points_and_pathways: pCA >65% and operable: surgical resection.
Pre-op tissue confirmation or for staging/biomarkers as indicated.
Not operable or nondiagnostic biopsy: SBRT.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: High probability of malignancy (pCA >65%) IPNs
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: If patient is not operable, consider nonsurgical options.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: SBRT for patients not able to undergo surgery or with nondiagnostic/not possible biopsy.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In those with high probability of malignancy (pCA > 65%), a referral to surgery for resection of the nodule is the standard of care
